If Saturn is situated in the third house from the Moon, it causes the destruction of one's brother;
yet it also makes a man like a king and a recipient of various pleasures.
Situated in the fourth house, the son of the Sun (Saturn) brings about bondage for men, as well as wealth and disease;
moreover, Saturn bestows residence at the edge of a village, deprived of wife, joy, and sons. (4)
If Saturn is in the fifth house or an enemy's sign, one becomes devoid of sons and wealth and suffers misery;
however, some say that if it is in its exaltation or a friend's sign, one becomes lame but possesses a son.

In the sixth house, Saturn bestows upon men base desires, fear of people, and destruction by enemies; however, when situated in its exaltation, it grants wealth, virtue, and desire, as well as diligent effort.

When Saturn is situated in the seventh house, it destroys all wealth and slays the wife; however, when it reaches its exaltation (Tuṅga) in a benefic sign, it grants a wife who is barren, harsh, and of short stature.
When Saturn is in the eighth house, a man remains in another country, possessing a beautiful form, joyful, and happy, though he experiences suffering.
When the Moon is conjoined with the Nidhana yoga, a person born under this configuration becomes a king who possesses pure dharma and is a benefactor to others;
he is endowed with fullness of body and large eyes, and he attains death at a most excellent sacred ford.

When Jupiter is in the house of Dharma (the ninth house), a man becomes pure, possessing a body that is like a vessel for visiting sacred pilgrimage sites, happy, and honored by hosts of gods and excellent brahmins; he enjoys great festivals through the fortune acquired by his own strength.
If Venus is in the tenth house, the native will have blood relations, suffer from disease,
and even when living in the forest, he will enjoy royal happiness and be endowed with a handsome appearance.

Residing in his own home while the son of Bhṛgu (Śukra) is present, he—endowed with excellent qualities, firm in his vows, possessing a body like that of the God of Love, a vessel of happiness, delighting in laughter, and pleasing to behold—shall become [prosperous]. || 11 ||
When Venus is situated in the twelfth house, a man becomes afflicted by disease in his first stage of life;
thereafter, his mind is intent on pride, and he remains perpetually emaciated, hairless, and soiled.
Thus ends the results of Venus.
If the lord of the ascendant is in the sixth house, there will be a constant increase in skin diseases and ailments of the name (durnāma) for men;
if [the lord] is either deficient or excessive, it bestows the lowest status within one's lineage.
If Mars is situated in the seventh house, one suffers from diseases of the eyes and stomach, and is emaciated by blood loss; in the eighth, wealth, honor, and life are exhausted;

and when Mars is placed in the ninth, one's progress is delayed by humiliation, loss of wealth, and other such misfortunes, as well as by physical ailments, lack of strength, and exhaustion of the bodily constituents.

When Mars is in the tenth house, there is the acquisition of various kinds of wealth; when it is in the ninth house, there is victory. When situated in the eleventh house, one enjoys the countryside like a forest with beautiful blossoming tops at its edge.
If Mars is in the twelfth house in Nānāvyaya, a person suffers from hundreds of misfortunes;
he is prone to anger toward women, possesses wealth, suffers from eye pain, and is arrogant toward cowherds.
Thus concludes the motion of Mars.
One whose wealth has been seized by wicked speech, sycophants, enemies, divisive persons, and those who cause imprisonment,
and who travels on foot because the lord of the birth sign and the Moon are in the sixth house, does not hear even a word of welcome or well-being.

When Venus is in the third house, there is the acquisition of wealth; however, if the Moon and Mercury are also there, one experiences heartache, loss of wealth, fear of enemies, anxiety, and incurs expenses.
The movement of the moon.
In the first half of Kuja-vighāta, there is suffering for the king; in the second half, it removes that suffering. In Dhā-kṛṣa, there is loss of wealth due to fire, thieves, and disease;
and in Upendra-vajra-pati, even the lord himself may suffer.
And when Mars is in the third house from the son of the thief (Mercury), it bestows results such as radiance,
authority, wealth, woolen garments, precious minerals, and various other things.
And when Venus is in the fourth house, it causes fever, abdominal diseases, blood disorders, and heavy debts, as well as misfortune arising from association with wicked men, even by force.
When the earth has given birth to a son who causes fear from enemies, poison, and anger, and who is afflicted by the five [senses] and the five [objects],
his splendor does not remain firm for long, just as a *mālatī* flower placed upon the head of a dog.

When Mars has gone to the house of an enemy, is he not fanned by the faces of women who are adorned with gold, coral, copper, and conch shells, and who are themselves free from fear of enemies, danger, and strife?
In the third house, there is the destruction of wife, arts, and honor; in the fourth, one suffers from many afflictions regarding kinsmen and wealth. (p.
52a) With Jupiter as the lord of the ninth, there is peace, wealth acquired through cows, and he enjoys the forest with his entire village, living a life of great longevity.

And Jupiter, having entered the house of children, produces for the master of the household auspicious sons, elephants, horses, and bulls, as well as golden cities, houses, young women, clothing, and a multitude of excellent jewels.
Neither the face of her friend, radiant with a forehead mark, nor the forest resounding with the cries of peacocks and cuckoos,
nor the ground variegated by the leaps of deer, brought any pleasure to the mind of Rukmiṇī as she gazed upon her husband.
The wealth, food, flowers, and sovereignty of the Teacher of the Thirty-three, which are to be enjoyed through rest and pleasure.
Occupying the seventh house from birth, she produces speech that is graceful and possesses the wisdom of a mountain-dweller (the sage Vālmīki).
In the eighth house, there is bondage, disease, intense sorrow, the hardships of travel, and diseases equal to death;
yet, through skillfulness, there is success in sons, dharma, and wealth. For women devoted to their husbands, there is the attainment of dharma;
however, in those of wicked conduct, they quickly go to a state of downfall.

When the Moon is in the fourth house, there is an increase in one's own kin and family, and the acquisition of wealth occurs; however, being situated in the fifth house, it causes conflict with sons and wife, and one does not enjoy even a beautiful woman.

In the sixth house, there is good fortune, victory, and prosperity; in the seventh, loss of caste and excessive quarreling; in the eighth, death; but when [the planet] is in the ninth, there is the attainment of victory, sons, clothing, wealth, skill, and immeasurable joy.

The ninth [lord], the son of the Moon (Mercury), causes obstacles; when situated in the tenth house, he destroys enemies and bestows wealth. He provides joy, a bed, stories of burning houses, and carpets.
Wealth, sons, happiness, women, friends, the attainment of one's word, contentment, and pleasing speech are obtained when the Moon is in the eleventh house.

If the Moon is in the twelfth house, one experiences the passion of being humiliated by enemies; one does not become an enjoyer of wealth, and there is happiness from the Mālinī yoga—thus says Budhavāra.
During his lifetime, he was deprived of wealth and intellect; through the loss of his position, he was reduced to poverty, and in his eighth year, he brought misfortune upon his wife and household.
In the ninth house, however, there will be a virtuous wife who partakes in happiness, as well as a collection of wealth and garments from Jupiter;
in the tenth house, due to the absence of strife, one obtains even measured words when speaking.
The son of Bhṛgu (Venus), situated in the penultimate house, bestows friends, wealth, food, and fragrance;
when situated in the eleventh house, it brings the acquisition of stable objects and excellent gains.
Thus ends the motion of Venus.
In the first *erāva* year, one is struck by poison or fire, separated from one's own kin, and commits the slaughter of a kinsman;
having gone to a foreign land, one finds happiness, wealth, sons, and fame in the house of a friend.
In the second house, by the influence of Mercury, there is physical beauty and pleasure; yet the body is devoid of pride and strength.
Wealth acquired through the merits of others is indeed unstable; like a fresh flower fallen from its stalk, it does not remain for long.
If Saturn is in the third house during its period, one obtains wealth, as well as attendants, camels, buffaloes, elephants, and donkeys;
there is happiness from the prosperity of one's home, the cessation of disease, and even for the timid, there is peace and an abundance of physical beauty.
In Lalita.
The fourth house is the house of fear;
even if a man is not arrogant, he goes to the twelfth house, which is a portion of suffering due to adverse circumstances.
Thus ends the movement of Jupiter.
The first house, occupied by the son of Bhṛgu (Venus), brings about an abundance of fragrant, charming-smelling flowers and fine garments for the sake of amorous enjoyment;
it also provides the pleasures of beds, houses, food, and seats, as well as the humming of bees at the lotus-faces of intoxicated, playful women.

When Venus is situated in the second house, one obtains offspring, wealth, grain, and the favor of kings; having acquired these beneficial things, even though his hair is as radiant as the *vasantatilaka* flower, he enjoys himself with the splendor of flowers and jewels at will.
If Jupiter is in the third house, he bestows honor, wealth, fine garments, and the destruction of enemies.
And in the fourth [foot], it bears a gathering of friends (suhṛtsamāja) and the upendravajrā-imparted power.
When Venus is situated in the fifth house, Jupiter bestows satisfaction, the acquisition of kinsmen,
sons, wealth, swift gains, friends, assemblies, food, and freedom from disease.
In the sixth house, Bhṛgu causes humiliation, grief, and distress; in the seventh, the inauspicious one produces [misfortune] caused by women.
If Mars is situated in the fifth house, it causes distress in the second and seventh houses, brings loss in the fourth and eighth houses, and bestows fear from children, enemies, and disease.

In the sixth house, [the Moon] causes the cessation of sons and wife; in the seventh, it is not excellent; in the eighth, there is danger from enemies; and situated in the ninth, it brings about affliction.
In the sixth house, one engages in sexual union with women and obtains stories for diversion; in the seventh, however, there is joy, satisfaction, and the acquisition of wealth.
In the eighth, eleventh, or twelfth house.
Thus ends the movement of Rāhu.
When Rāhu is in the first, eighth, tenth, sixth, or third house, this various moving result is the attainment of wealth;
it always bestows health, victory, happiness, stability, and the increase of one's kinsmen.
Rāhu, wandering here in the second, seventh, ninth, fourth, or twelfth house from birth, causes great suffering.
It brings about mounting, the crushing of enemies, the destruction of wealth, disease, exile, death, and fierce disputes.
The Nāhuścāra is completed.
When [the Moon] is in the house of Saturn, one is separated from friends, wealth, wife, and so forth;
and one's wealth becomes as crooked as a serpent and is like a snake that has gone away.
If Saturn is in the fifth house, one is bereft of learning and wealth and is beset by intense quarrels;
yet, when it occupies the sixth house, the leader of enemies is utterly destroyed, and its face is adorned with a beautiful smile and lips like a vessel of fortune.
He proceeds to the seventh and eighth meditations; devoid of wife and son, he is free from the exertion of worldly activity.
Likewise, through the firmness of dharma, his heart is bound by the dharma that cuts away all suffering, and the Goddess of Action performs her rites today.
In the tenth house from Saturn, there is the attainment of dharma and the destruction of wealth; in the eleventh and twelfth houses, there is the loss of knowledge and honor.
In the second house, one attains sharp gains and the acquisition of wealth from others, yet at the end, one encounters a succession of waves of sorrow.
Thus ends the movement of Saturn.
In the first [house], there is indeed the affliction of poison from enemies; in the second, there is the attainment of camphor, agallochum, fragrant garments, and victory;
in the third, there is gain for men—such is the characteristic of the mind.
From the *ruya* [nakṣatra] to the *ṛkṣa* [nakṣatra], the *gaṇḍa* belongs to the Pitṛ-devatā; wherever that *gaṇḍa* may occur, it exists within those five *bhelas*.
That is to be known as the fourth fixed yoga (dhruva-yoga); it is called Ṣaṣṭhī when [the moon] is in the sixth [nakṣatra], and Vaidhṛti occurs in the tenth. Furthermore, Viṣṭi occurs in the sixth.
The four ghaṭikās beginning with Vyāghāta, all the [other] aniṣṭa [muhūrtas], Dhruva, and Dhṛti,
as well as Bhiṣa and Gaṇḍa— these should each be considered for one muhūrta as the pāta (fall) of the Sun.
Brahmā fell from his flight, Hari fell from his flight, and Śambhu fell from his flight; therefore, one should avoid such a fall.
Thus ends the section on falling.
If the planets beginning with Vidyādinanātha are situated on a single line,
then in that marriage, the bride shall never live.
Thus, having deliberated upon the five-pronged diagram (pañcaśalākā), one should avoid piercing [the auspicious points]:
in the case of a solar piercing (ravivedha), there is widowhood; in the case of a Martian piercing (kujavedha), there is the destruction of the family.
The letters va, u, dha, dha, dhe, bha, ve, and dhaṃ are to be excluded from the meditation on Jupiter due to piercing.
If Venus is pierced [by a malefic], she is childless; if the Moon is pierced, she is miserable.
If Mars is pierced, she is devoted to another's husband; if Rāhu or Ketu is pierced, she wanders at will.
Thus is the piercing.
In whichever house the Moon and a planet may be, and likewise when there is an eclipse or an equality of declination (*krāntisāmya*),
as well as the "burnt" lunar day (*dagdhātithi*)— these ten defects are known to be of great power.
Having abandoned these due to their inauspiciousness, the wise man should carefully examine the auspicious moment (lagna).
The Sun is in the twelfth (12) house, Mars in the third (3),
Jupiter in the sixth (6), and Saturn in the eighth (8).
When the moon is situated in the eastern quarter, O Goddess, the planets beginning with the Moon are arranged in reverse order;
Rāhu (the son of Siṃhikā) should be placed in the twenty-second asterism (22), and Ketu (the son of Siṃhikā) in the ninth (9).
In the seventh house, Venus is the son of Soma; likewise, in the fifth house, there shall be loss of wealth due to the Sun, Mars, Rāhu, and Saturn.
O beloved, death occurs during the period of life, and there shall be the loss of kinsmen.
Through Venus, there is the failure of one's duties; through Mercury, misfortune;
and through the Moon, great terror—the fruit of a blow from a kick is thus recorded.
Thus ends the section on the kick.
The wheel of the *pāta* (falling) is determined from the lunar mansion occupied by the Sun:
Maghā, Āśleṣā, Citrā, Anurādhā, and Revatī.
This group of six asterisms, beginning with Śravaṇā, is declared to be defiled by fall (pāta). One should count them starting from Aśvinī up to the zodiacal sign (lagna) in question.
Pāvaka, Pāvamāna, Vikāra, Kalahotpara, and Mṛtyukṣaya—these are to be known as the six *pātas*. Beyond this, O Goddess, in the *śalākācakra*, one is liberated from the divisions;
listen, O beloved, as I describe it according to the divisions of the earth.
One should especially deliberate upon matters such as the commencement of battle;
[one should consult] the wheel known as the *saptaśalākā*, which reveals the results of both the auspicious and the inauspicious.
There are seven lines from east to west and likewise seven from south to north;
upon these, one should place the asterisms beginning with Kṛttikā in their proper sequence.
Following the sequence starting from the east, there are twenty-eight in number;
among them, this one is to be meditated upon as the Gauri-dagdha-liṅga, which is smoky-colored.
Listen, O beloved, as I describe the piercing [of the body] by means of the placement of the planets.

In that regard, O beloved, one should know a constellation joined with a malefic planet to be "embraced" (āliṅgita); one should designate that which has a malefic planet standing upon it as "bound" (akhastambha). That which is released by a malefic planet is "burnt" (dagdha), and that which stands before it is "smoky" (vidhūmita).
In the *āliṅgita* yoga, there is fear from both sides and disease; in *sammukha*, there is the destruction of the family.
In *hata* and *dagdha*, death occurs, and likewise, in *uddhūmita*, there is defeat.
Lattā, pāta, yuti, vedha, yāmitra, and budha— these five are inauspicious; however,
ekārgala is auspicious in the third house, while vijaya is auspicious in the sixth and eleventh houses, being equal [in effect] to them.
When the wind has set out, it constantly brings about the acquisition of clothing, wealth, gold, and friends for those who are well-disposed toward their kin.

Ketu, situated in the second, twelfth, fifth, ninth, fourth, seventh, eighth, or tenth house from the birth ascendant, constantly causes distress, grief, fear, obstacles, and the destruction of one's goals; it perpetually brings about intense humiliation.
Thus ends the movement of the comet.
One should establish five lines on the cord, likewise facing transversely;
and two by two at each of the four corners, there is a wheel with five spokes.
Kṛttikā should be assigned to Īśāna, and the other lunar mansions in their proper sequence;
the planets should be assigned to them, and one should deliberate upon the auspicious and inauspicious results.

The last quarter of the asterism called Vaiśvadeva (Anurādhā) and the first three quarters of Viṣṇu’s asterism (Śravaṇā) are declared to be the four [units] known as Bhukti; when a planet is situated therein, it pierces the asterism Rohiṇī along with Abhijit.
Thus ends the section on the five sticks.
p. 57a) It is in the Vaidhatī [nakṣatra].
The [nakṣatras] named Āditya, Candra, Pitṛ, Sarpa, Bhadra, Sumūla, Maitra, Ākhyāti, Tiṣya, Suravardhani, and Bhāni are located in the head.
One should establish thirteen lines extending upward from the top and likewise thirteen extending horizontally; this wheel is called the *kārdūrika* by the wise.
Among these, the "strikes" (*vyāghāta*) and so forth are said to occur where two lines meet at the top.
The conjunction of the sun and the moon, as described in the *mithuna* [aspect], is called the *ekārgala* configuration.
A certain fierce man of deformed body, born from the collision of the gaze of the sun and the rays of the moon,

falls into the midst of the world for the destruction of auspicious things; indeed, he burns the worlds with a gaze tawny like fire— your one eye is the second fire, and your third eye is the fourth earth.
The foot of the yogin is joined with the *viti* and *ūrk*, and the lunar conjunction is at the foot of the *bha*.
The lunar asterisms are divided, in reverse order, by one, two, three, four, and five asterisms belonging to the solar asterisms, respectively.
Thus ends the "Single Bolt."
Thus are the ten defects.
O Deluder of the World!
Those [planets] declared to cause obstacles in their own places are censured in all undertakings;
in marriage, there would be loss of life, and on a journey, death would certainly occur.
Then the defect of conjunction (yuti-doṣa) is to be known; it destroys both the auspicious and inauspicious [effects].
Joined with Rāhu, it causes loss; joined with Mars, it brings about death; and joined with Rāhu, Ketu, and Saturn, it effects the destruction of the very root of the body.
Thus ends the conjunction.
The fourteenth lunar mansion is known as Yāmitra; it is considered the portion of the ascendant.
They desire it when conjoined with a benefic planet, and one should avoid it when conjoined with a malefic.
The Moon, Venus, Jupiter, Mercury, and Mars are friends and benefactors; the Sun, Saturn, and Rahu grant auspiciousness through friendship with their own lords.
If planets— excluding the Sun— are situated in the fourteenth house from either the Moon or the Ascendant,
they will certainly cause disease and widowhood.
Thus ends the section on the *jāmitra*.
The values for the year (15), month (12), and period (10) should be added to the days elapsed since the last solar transit (saṃkrānti).
When divided by the [number of] planets, if the result is five, there will be disease; likewise, if it is four, fire; if three, poverty; and if two, death.
Thus ends the group of five [planets] beginning with Mercury.

In the case of an odd yoga-number, one (1) is to be added; in the case of an even number, twenty-eight (28). Having halved [the result], the asterism Aśvinī is first subtracted, and the resulting nakṣatra is placed at the head.
Having released the afflictions of Vyāghāta, Śūla, Parigha, Vyatipāta, Gaṇḍa, Atigaṇḍa, Kuliśa, and Iṣu,
Saturn [proceeds].
Thus ends the Śanichakra.

One should place [the nakṣatras] at the head of the service-wheel (sevācakra), seven on the chest and belly, and likewise seven on the two feet; among them, one should assign Ṛkṣa, Aṇi, Sā, and Abhijit.
The asterism of the master (svāmibha) should be counted from the asterism of the servant (bhṛtyabha), and then from the asterism of the servant back to the asterism of the master;
that which is situated on the back of the feet is fruitless, while that which is on the head or the belly yields fruit.
Thus ends the wheel of service.
One should assign the lunar mansions according to the three wheels: three at the head, beginning with Bhānu;
two on the face; two on the shoulders; and one each on the arms and hands.
There is one group of six [syllables] each in the heart, navel, and secret place;
one at the knees and elbows; and likewise one each in the two feet; wherever [these are placed], there is that fruit.

If it is located on the head, there is the acquisition of an umbrella; if in the mouth, the eating of sweet food; if in the neck, wealth; and if in the shoulder, the man shall be displaced from his position.

In the two hands, there is the misfortune of being a thief; in the heart, there is little lifespan and fear; in the private parts, there is lust and wandering; and in the feet, there is a meager livelihood.
Thus ends the *Triṃbhacakra*.
One should draw a plough-shaft together with two yokes;
on the shaft, one should write the twelve signs starting from the sign occupied by the Sun at the time of birth.
In the case of oxen yoked to poles and plows, there should be two pairs at each position and three at the third; likewise, there should be three for the two traces.
One should avoid an ox that is joined with such a configuration when sowing seeds, commencing the building of a house, or gathering grain.
(p. 58b) One should likewise avoid an ox associated with an *upagraha* [malefic conjunction].
Upagraha, Mahādoṣa, Bhūmika, and Pādayogya should always be avoided during auspicious rites; they are like the Kālakūṭa poison.
Having drawn the Saturn-wheel (Śanīcakra) in human form, starting from the sign of Scorpio (Saura),
one should know that whatever name or lunar mansion (ṛkṣa) falls upon it, therein lies the auspicious or inauspicious result.
One on the mouth, four on the right arm,
five on the left arm, four on the head, three on the eyes, and two each on the private parts and the anus.
Victory in speech when [Saturn] is in the mouth; skill when in the right hand; delusion in the feet; prosperity in the heart;
fear in the left hand; sovereignty in the head; happiness of the eyes; and death in the anus.
When Saturn causes obstacles in the first, eighth, or twelfth houses from the ascendant:
Then that [suffering] exists in the body through the heart, head, eyes, and the ten [limbs].
When Saturn brings happiness in the third, first, tenth, and sixth houses,
then there is no obstacle regarding bodily ailments, nor diseases of the private parts, the mouth, or the neck.
For one whom Śauri causes affliction, this wheel should clearly be drawn with black substances and cast by a wise person into the midst of oil.
Having placed [the object] in the middle of the ground, one should worship it with black flowers;
it will attain satisfaction, of this there is no doubt. Uttarā, Ārdrā, Maghā, Bharaṇī, as well as Aśleṣā and Kṛttikā—these are certainly the constellations of departure and death.
Vi 53 ma ābha aśleṣā kṛttikā.
The fruit of death by an inferior journey.
1. Now follows the determination of the lunar day for a journey.
On the first day, one should partake of sun-leaves; on the second, betel-leaf and water;
on the third, ghee; and on the fourth, jaggery and grain.
On the fifth day, water; on the sixth, water with a discus;
on the seventh, water with a skull; on the eighth, *bījapūraka* (citron);
on the ninth, water with a skull; and on the tenth lunar day, cow’s urine.
On the eleventh day, one should subsist on barley; on the twelfth day, one should eat flour.
On the thirteenth day, one should consume sesame; on the fourteenth, oil-cake;
and on the full moon day, kṛśara (rice and pulse mixture)—this is auspicious and brings success to one’s journey.
Now follows the consumption [of food] under the lunar mansions.
Having consumed curd under Kṛttikā, one should likewise consume kṛśara under Rohiṇī.
Under Mṛgaśīrṣā, one should eat deer meat; under Ārdrā, one should observe the blood-vow (rudhiravrata); under Punarvasu, patola gourds; and under Puṣya, ghee and milk-rice.
In Aśleṣā, one should eat sesame and meat; in Madyā, one should have a meal of Sāri.
On the full moon of Phālguna, there are two [offerings] on the five-pointed [fire].

If the asterism is situated on the staff, there is loss of cattle; if it is situated on the yoke, both [loss of cattle and wealth] belong to the owner. If it is situated on the plow or the thong, there is prosperity at the commencement of the field-work.
There will be gain on the eighth day, but on the ninth there is affliction by weapons; one should never go [on the tenth], for it brings association with death.
The attainment of the tenth bhūmi occurs on the tenth day, and likewise on the eleventh;
on the twelfth day one should proceed, and on the thirteenth all perfections are achieved.
Whether it be on the dark or the bright [fortnight], the thirteenth day is successful for all; however, one should prohibit travel on the fourteenth and the full moon day.
Thus ends the section on the lunar days (tithi).
Aśvinī, Anurādhā, Revatī, Mṛgaśīrṣa, Mūla, Punarvasu, Puṣya, Hasta, and likewise Jyeṣṭhā— these are said to be the most excellent among the best nakṣatras.
The horse, the bull, the deer, the flower, and the supreme.
The supreme journey.
The three stars beginning with Rohiṇī, Svāti, Citrā, Vāruṇa (Śatabhiṣaj), Śravaṇā, and Dhaniṣṭhā constitute the middle path, which is immortality.
Ro pū 3 svā ci śa śra dha.
The journey begins with the middle [channel].
This is proclaimed as the yoga of Viśākhā.
On the day of *vyatīpāta*, honey-water; on the day of *varīyas*, wheat-rice;
on the day of *parigha*, curd-rice and auspicious betel-leaf.
White mustard seeds should be consumed for the attainment of *siddhi*, and a snake-king for the attainment of *sādhya*.
One should partake of auspicious food; this is proclaimed as the "Śukrapadya" [fast].
The ten roots of Brahmaśīrṣa, along with aindrī and marica,
when combined with honey during the Vaidhṛti yoga, bestow the fruit of hearing and understanding the meaning of the Vedas.
Alternatively, there is the consumption of the [planetary] day.
The Sun [is represented by] water brought from a lake; the Moon, by a mirror; Mars, by saffron; Mercury, by coriander and white mustard seeds.
Adhika, Haritavya, Śukra, Kapura, Rājika, Sūryaputra, Vigaṅga, and Tiśita bestow the desired [results].
Now follows the consumption of the first-fruits (lagnaprāśana).
In the month of Mīna, one should offer red sandalwood mixed with curd and honey;
in Vṛṣa, red sandalwood; in Mithuna, red sandalwood; and in Karkaṭaka, water with kṛsara (rice and sesame).
In Leo, the fruit of the atiphala is prescribed; in Virgo, cow's milk and water are praised; in Libra, aquatic products; and in Scorpio, barley flour.
In the sign of Cancer, one should offer lotus filaments; in Leo, sesamum and liṅgas;
in Virgo, makara fish; in Libra, taṇḍula rice; in Scorpio, goat's milk; and in Sagittarius, milk-porridge.
Now follows the ritual of tasting the directions.
In the east, there is molasses and cakes; likewise in the north, vegetables; in the hand [of the moon], millet as food; and under Citrā, various kinds of diverse meals.
In Svāti, one should consume meat; in Viśākhā, well-prepared food;
in Anurādhā, peas; and in Jyeṣṭhā, boiled rice with ghee.
Under Mūla one should consume radish; under Pūrvāṣāḍhā, one should drink water;
under Uttarāṣāḍhā, one should drink milk; and from Śravaṇa onwards, one should take sugar.
In Vāśavaṃśāli there is Niryāsa; in Vāruṇa, Kulatthaka;
in Keśala there is Bhadrapada; and in Mūrttarā, Māṃsavārāha.
In Revatī, food mixed with beans; in Aśvinī, goat's milk;
in Bharaṇī, a field of sesame—then the journey will be auspicious.
Now follows the consumption of the yoga-mixture.
In the Viṣkambha yoga, kṛśara is prescribed; in Prīti, rice with jaggery;
in Āyuṣmān, black gram; and in Saubhāgya, parched grain.
In Śobhana, one should give tubi-linga; in Atigaṇḍa, vasānaka;
in Sukarman, one should give nitila; and for Dhṛti, one should designate upakṣiṇa.
In Śūla, one gives śālmalī seeds, and in Gaṇḍa, apāmārga.
Likewise, Vṛddhauśanas, Vyeva, Dhruva, and Sarīsṛpa;

In the case of a clash, they know that there will be a threshing of *kulattha* beans; one should avoid [such a time]. One should eat sweet food when seeing a prepared meal, a heap of grain, a pot-bearer, one wearing red flowers and garments, a madman, an empty jar, a quarrel taking place in front, or a load of wood. (p. 66a)
If there is neither death nor success for men who have set out on their journey, [what then?]
Whatever auspicious or inauspicious signs there are for those departing on their journey, even those found in dreams—
whether good or bad— the smearing with excrement is considered auspicious.

Some say that the cry of a bird beyond the distance of one *krośa* is fruitless; in such a case, if the first omen is unfavorable, one should wait for five *ghaṭikās*. For inauspicious omens, a king should perform sixteen *prāṇāyāmas*; likewise, he should return [to his position] on the second [attempt].
If he is unwilling to go from his own abode, that is the third [case].
All the omens have been explained by the sages as being highly auspicious.
The three—Aśastra, Śarakuṃbha, and Śṛgālaka—are excluded.
One should avoid one who has unfinished business, one who lacks medicine, one who possesses black grain, salt, or a neck-tie;
one who has oil on their body, one who is naked, one who is raw (uncooked), one who is ignorant, one who carries jujube fruit, honey, or a snake;

one who wears a hide, one who is impure, one who is hot, one who is afflicted by disease, one who is blind, one who is intoxicated, one with matted hair, one who carries wood, one who carries grass, one who is covered in dust, one who carries buttermilk, one who is bald, one who is smeared with oil, and one whose hair has fallen out.
And those ending in -kākhādyaṇa are inauspicious.
Thus ends the section on festivals.
In the south-eastern direction, one should offer a pomegranate together with wine;
in the western part, a fish; and in the north, meat.
A cow, a maiden, a conch, a kettledrum, curd, fruit, a flower, glowing barley-gruel,
a vehicle, an umbrella, a chariot, a king, a radiant light, a full water-pot,
a twice-born man, the earth being lifted up, a pair of moving aquatic creatures, food signifying success, a hundred-year-old woman, a courtesan, a wife, and meat.
Even speech that is burdensome is commendable for those who have set out on their journey.

White mustard seeds, eleven lotuses, a jar filled with poison, a jar filled with water, a turban, a water-pot, a half-moon, heaps of grain, a new garment, and a sunshade— these are the auspicious articles.
Curd, honey, ghee, eyes, a mark on the forehead, a conch, a banner, a lotus, a water-jar, a lotus, an auspicious seat,
a conch, a white bull, flowers, garments, a fish, a group of twice-born, a courtesan, and a beloved wife are the signs of the western quarter;
as are a blazing fire, fruit, unbroken rice, a horse, an elephant, a clay drum, kusha grass, a chowrie, and weapons.
Various kinds of jewels, headed by emeralds, kuruvilvas, rubies, and crystal gems.
Now, that which is not praiseworthy:
One should visualize [the victim] as intoxicated, smeared with oil, naked, with disheveled hair, and crying out "piśukha";
then, having recited "Oṃ namaḥ sūryāya," [one should strike him]. (p. 67a, 1)
Indeed, the results of the periods (daśās) of those planetary heaps, which are like a wheel of auspicious and inauspicious karma,
as well as the various results of their houses, lunar mansions, and horās, have been declared.
The solar period.
He spoke of the auspicious and inauspicious [results] of the three nakṣatras: Kṛttikā, Uttaraphalgunī, and Uttarāṣāḍhā.
Fever, constellations, and diseases of the eighth month.

Year 1, month 4: auspicious. Year 2: danger from stomach ailments and fire. Year 2, month 8: danger from kings, falling objects, fire, and stomach ailments. Year 4: acquisition of clothing and wealth. Year 4: danger from poison and fire. Year 4, month 8: middling results. Year 1, month 4: various diseases. Year 6: acquisition of various ornaments and other goods.
For seven years and two months, there will be the onset of phlegm-induced fever.

In the eighth year and third month, there is danger from blood dysentery and fire. In the ninth year and fourth month, there is danger from horned animals. In the tenth year and sixth month, there is gain of all objectives. In the eleventh year and seventh month, there is great suffering. In the twelfth year and seventh month, it is auspicious. In the thirteenth year and ninth month, there is the suffering of exile.
At 11 years and 10 months, there will be the attainment of a wife and prosperity. At 16 years and 9 months, there will be a wound from a weapon inflicted by a thief.
At 17 years and 6 months, there will be fear of poison and disease. At 18 years and 4 months, there will be the attainment of a son. At 19 years and [4] months...

In the [first] year, there will be no danger from women; in the 19th year and 10th month, there will be the disease of burning fever; in the 20th year and 7th month, loss of sons and wealth; in the 21st year and 4th month, the birth of a daughter; in the 22nd year and 2nd month, fear of the king’s wrath.

In the 23rd year, there is gain from women’s wealth. In the 24th year, fear of kings, falls, and fire. In the 25th year, illness. In the 26th year, the birth of a son. In the 27th year, favor from the king. In the 28th year, gain of one’s own kinsmen and friends. In the 29th year, loss of sons and wealth. In the 30th year, gain of learning and wealth. In the 31st year, moderate results. In the 32nd year, death or imprisonment.

Year 33: Fear; the giving away of a son; conflict. Year 34: Attainment of desires; joined with sons and wife. Year 36: Great fear. Year 37: Conflict within the family. Year 38: Gain of wealth through a woman.

In the 39th year, there will be success through friends. In the 40th year, there will be misfortune and conflict. In the 41st year, however, there will be threefold distress and anger. In the 42nd year, for ten months, there will be the acquisition of various objects.

Year 43, month 7: loss of one's residence in Kuru. Year 44, month 7: suffering from wind-disorders and diarrhea. Year 45, month 7: conflict with brothers. Year 46, month 7: affliction by fever and intoxication. Year 47: strife within the circle of servants. Year 48, month 4: fear of thieves in the family. Year 49.
In the *Rahasya* and other [texts], there is gain through the knowledge of women; prosperity and auspiciousness for 50 years and 2 months;

honor from the king for 50 years and 2 months; fear from many sources for 51 years and 11 months; gain of jewels for the 52nd year; auspiciousness for 9 months of the 53rd year; great calamity for 9 months of the 54th year; fear of displacement for the 55th year; and [the period] of 6 months of the 56th year.
Wounds in the region of the head; loss of wealth in the 57th year; if he dies at 58 years and 3 months, his maximum lifespan is 60 years—he lives for sixty years. The Sun’s Dasa is concluded. (7)

He states the results of the Moon's period (candradāśā): In Rohiṇī, Hasta, and Śravaṇa: 1 year and 2 months of fever and suffering from wind (vāta). In the next: 2 years and 3 months of fever, abdominal pain, and worms. In the next: 3 years and 7 months of sorrow and loss of wealth. In the next: 3 years and 6 months of obtaining clothing and ornaments. In the next: 7 years and 9 months of fever, colic, and dysentery.

p. 68b) In the 8th year and 11th month, for the sake of obtaining cattle and land; in the 9th year, moderate gain; in the 10th year, suffering from fever and eye ailments; in the 10th year and 9th month, danger from poison, fire, and leprosy; in the 11th year and 6th month, sudden conflict; in the 12th year and 5th month, gain through association with women; in the 13th year and 3rd month, various fears and sorrows.

Year 13, month 10: auspicious. Year 14, month 7: anxiety regarding kinsmen. Year 15, month 5: gain of a wife. Year 16, month 2: fear of the king, stones, and wood; at the end, there is gain. Year 17: gain of a daughter. Year 18: fear of weapons. Year 19: fear of various diseases, quarrels, and so forth. Year 21: gain of learning for the sake of a son.
In the twenty-third year: loss of various objects and distress. In the twenty-fourth year: gain of wealth and grain. In the twenty-sixth and twenty-seventh years:
great sorrow, disease, and suffering. In the twenty-ninth year: happiness, wealth, glory, and good fortune. In the thirty-first year: fear of kings and thieves.
In the thirty-third year, there is honor from friends engaged in ritual activities. In the thirty-fourth year, suffering arises due to women.

In the 36th year and 10th month, there will be gain of sons, knowledge, clothing, and food. In the 37th year and 7th month, there will be great illness and loss of family wealth. In the 60th year and 4th month, there will be gain due to relief from the affliction of Āśleṣā. In the 42nd year and 1st month, there will be fear of conflict with son and wife, leprosy, and skin diseases. In the 43rd year and 11th month, there will be protection for the wife and gain of a daughter.

Gain of position: at 54 years and 4 months, gain from the king, fire, fever, and dysentery. Gain of various objects: at 47 years and 6 months. Fear of weapons, thieves, loss of wealth, and disease: at 49 years and 3 months.

Year 41: a period of obstacles. Year 42: moderate results. Year 53 and 1 month: suffering from living abroad. Year 54: gain of cattle. Year 55 and 2 months: gain of wealth and grain. Year 56: conflict. Year 57 and 3 months: auspicious for learning and wealth. Year 58: prosperity. Year 59 and 5 months: gain of all desired objects. Year 60: [omitted].
Great suffering; in the 51st year and 5th month, separation from kinsmen; in the 52nd year, gain of an elderly woman; in the 53rd year and 6th month, fever and royal honors.
30 years and 6 months: suffering from women and children. 32 years and 3 months: the period (daśā) of the Chidra-sampat.

Year 33: A period of adversity. Year 34: Attainment of the desired object of a son. Year 35: Loss of the desired object of a son. Year 36: Departure for travel for one month. Year 37: A period of adversity. Year 38: Gain from trade for one month. Year 39: Fear of cattle and fire. Year 40: Conflict with one's own kinsmen for one month. Year 41: Attainment of a daughter. Year 42.
The attainment of various goals; in the 43rd year, the theft of household goods on account of a woman; in the 44th year, the loss of various objects and illness.
Forty-five years and two months: auspicious. Forty-six years and one month: fulfillment of desires. Forty-seven years: great danger.

In the 48th year, loss of various possessions. In the 39th year, for two months, danger from falling buildings and fire, as well as conflict. In the 40th year, exile and grief for kinsmen. In the 51st year, auspiciousness. In the 52nd year, attainment of great wealth. In the 53rd year, for eleven months, suffering from fever and wind-related ailments. In the 55th year, for nine months, loss of family members.
p. 70, 71?? p. 72a) In the 57th year and 7th month, there is auspiciousness. In the 59th year and 5th month, there is the danger of an outbreak of fever.
Fortunate: 61 years and 4 months. The period of deficiency (cchidra-daśā): 63 years and 7 months. If one dies during this time, the maximum lifespan is 73 years;
one lives for seventy-three years. The results of Rāhu’s own period (sva-daśā) are completed.

The results of the period (daśā) of Vṛhaspati are stated as follows: In Punarvasu, Viśākhā, and Pūrvabhādrapadā: Year 1, Month 1: Gain of gold, clothing, and other such items. Year 2: Suffering from fever and skin diseases. Year 3, Month 7: Poisoning, danger from fire, falling from a height, and various diseases. Year 4: Auspicious. Year 5, Month 4: Fever and diseases of the private parts. Year 7, Month 1: [Auspicious].

Fever, eye disease, grief, and loss of wealth [occur]. In the 8th year and 11th month, there is the gain of great wealth. In the 10th year and 7th month, there is gain despite fever and diarrhea. In the 12th year and 6th month, there is the gain of wealth from women and happiness. In the middle of the 13th year, it is moderate. In the 14th year and 3rd month, there is injury from oneself and abdominal disease. In the middle of the 15th year, it is moderate. In the 16th year, there are various diseases. In the 17th year...
Conflict with one's own kinsmen for eighteen years and one month; conflict with the wife's kinsmen.
Year 19: Mid-year. Year 20: February; wind-fever and diarrhea. Year 21: Attainment of all goals.

22nd year, 3rd month: auspicious. 23rd year, 4th month: attainment of the desire for the enjoyment of women. 24th year: a period of obstacles. 26th year, 6th month: gain of cattle, gold, and so forth. 27th year: middling. 28th year, 8th month: gain of clothing, food, women, and drink. 29th year: loss of sons and wealth, displacement from one's position. 30th year, 9th month.
From the king, thieves, and weapons; the thirty-first year is auspicious; the thirty-second year, for ten months, is a period of decline characterized by fever, bile disorders, and the like.

In the thirty-third year, there is the attainment of knowledge for the sake of a son. In the thirty-fourth year, there is the acquisition of a kingdom. In the thirty-fifth year, there is a swelling of the testicles.
The three realms are disturbed. Year 36, month 11: the middling period. Year 37: the extremely difficult major period (ativakudaśā). Year 38, month 9:
the painful period of separation and conflict (viyogra duḥkhadaśā). Year 40, month 8: gain in all undertakings. Year 41: increase in quarrels and strife.
Death by water after forty-two years and six months.
Year 43: Prosperity through women’s wealth (*strīdhana*). Year 44, month 4: Fear of horned animals (*vaṣaśṛṅgin*). Year 45:
Fear of a major disease (*mahāvyādhi*). Year 46, month 3: Acquisition of various goods and wealth. Year 47: A period of ill fortune (*kudaśā*).

Year 48, month 1: excessive suffering. Year 49: auspicious. Year 50: gain of various objects. Year 50, month 9: danger from poison, anger, and fire. Year 51, month 7: gain of cattle and land. Year 52, month 5: affliction from fever, headache, and the king. Year 53, month 2: gain of all grains and other goods. Year 53, month 11.

Sudden conflict. Year 54, month 8: middling results. Year 55, month 6: gain of merit, wealth, fame, and good fortune. Year 56, month 3: suffering from separation from one's kinsmen and wife. Year 57: mixed results. Year 58: auspicious. Year 59, month 4: gain of various objects. Year 60: loss of reputation and wealth.
Year 61, month 6: various gains. Year 62: moderate. Year 63: suffering from phlegm and fever.

Year 64: Period of obstacles (*cchidradaśā*). Year 65: Middling. Year 66: Danger of bloody dysentery (*raktātisāra*). Year 67: Auspicious. Year 68: Great affliction. Year 69: Gain. Year 70: Auspicious. Year 72: If not death [then] excellent; he lives for eighty-four years. These are the results of Jupiter’s own period (*svadaśā*).

[The section] is completed. Now he states the results of Śaura’s own period (daśā): In the first year, under Puṣya, Anurādhā, and Uttara-bhadrā: fever and stomach disease. In the second year, for one month: fever, dysentery, and separation from kinsmen. In the third year: fever and pain in the private parts. In the fourth year, for two months: gain. In the fifth year: danger from poison, lightning, and fire. In the sixth year...

In the third year, there will be gain from the meaning of the scriptures (śāstrārtha). In the eighth year and eighth month, there will be gain of cattle, gold, and so forth. The ninth year is middling. In the tenth year and sixth month, there will be fever and eye disease. The eleventh year is middling. In the twelfth year, there will be gain from the meaning of the scriptures. The thirteenth year is middling. In the fourteenth year and third month, there is fear of poison, injury, and bloody diarrhea. The fifteenth year is auspicious.
Year 16, month 10: Sudden conflict. Year 17: Attainment of wealth through a son. Year 18:

Attainment of wealth through knowledge. Year 19: Fulfillment of desires. Year 20, month 11: [Period of] the middle. Year 22, month 9: Attainment of wealth through a son. Year 23: Attainment of wealth from a wife. Year 24, month 8: On account of a woman.
The twenty-fifth year: suffering, with anxiety due to fear of kings and thieves. The twenty-seventh year: auspicious. The twenty-eighth year, fifth month:
danger from horned animals and untimely death. The twenty-ninth year: an evil period (kudaśā). The thirtieth year, fourth month: great danger from weapons and fire.
Year 31: Suffering from grief for a woman and fear. Year 32: In the middle of the second month. Year 33: Acquisition of various objects.

Year 34, month 1: fear of the provocation of the three humors (tridhātu). Year 35: fear of great suffering. Year 36: sorrow and distress due to living abroad. Year 37: attainment of all branches of knowledge and so forth. Year 38, month 4: fear of the falling of arrows upon the head. Year 39, month 2: attainment of wealth through wife and sons. Year 40, month 8.
The period of vulnerability: year 41, month 6; [there will be] learning, satisfaction, protection, and gain.

Year 42, month 4: Loss of wealth due to faults. Year 46: Middling. Year 47, month 5: Destruction of sons, wife, and wealth; yet gain. Year 48: Auspicious. Year 49, month 9: A period of ill fortune (kudaśā). Year 50: Middling. Year 51, month 11: A period of great hardship (mahākaṣṭa-daśā). Year 52: Middling. Year 53: Auspicious.

The 54th year is auspicious. The 55th year is middling. In the 56th year, for four months, there is gain through learning. The 57th year is a period of bad planetary influence (kudaśā). The 58th year, for seven months, is a period of very bad influence (atikudaśā). The 59th year is middling. The 60th year, for one month, is auspicious.
If he does not die at sixty-two years, his maximum lifespan is seventy-two years; he lives for seventy-two years. The sixteenth [regnal] year of Śauri is completed.
He states the sixteen-year results for Mercury: In the first year, 11 months:

fever, abdominal disease, loss of appetite, and fear of fire. In the second year: moderate results. In the third year, 9 months: various types of news. In the fourth year: various fears. In the fifth year, 8 months: auspicious. In the sixth year: auspicious. In the seventh year, 5 months: fever and dysentery.

Year 9, month 4: auspicious. Year 10: middling. Year 11, month 1: fear of kings and fire. Year 12: gain. Year 13, month 3: evil period (kudaśā). Year 14: gain of women, clothing, and so forth. Year 15, month 2: middling. Year 16: sorrow and distress. Year 17, month 9: loss of children and wealth. Year 18.
For seven months, there will be prosperity through women, wealth, and jewels. For nineteen years and four months, there will be fear of kings and enemies, and the danger of untimely death.
In the 21st year and 8th month, there is fear of falling from a height and fire. In the 22nd year and 6th month, there is gain of wealth through a son's learning and royal favor.

Year 23, month 3: Loss of various possessions, affliction by enemies, and sorrow. Year 24: Mixed results. Year 25: Gain of cattle, land, and women. Year 26, month 1: Loss of wealth due to a woman. Year 27: Fear of thieves and fire. Year 28, month 6: Moderate results. Year 30, month 9: Happiness and prosperity. Year...
31. Fear of snakes, thieves, and fire; 32. For eleven months of the year, fear of the suffering of exile.
Year 33: Excessive negligence. Year 34: Middling. Year 35, month 1: No gain.

The 36th year is auspicious. The 37th year, for four months, brings loss of everything. The 38th year brings the destruction of livestock. The 39th year, for seven months, brings great sorrow and suffering. The 40th year brings gain of wealth and auspicious matters. The 41st year, for ten months, brings various gains. The 42nd year is middling. The 43rd year brings exile and great fear. The 44th year, for eight months, brings fever and eye disease. The 45th year—

Month 4: Gain of various objects. Year 46, Month 8: Extremely unfavorable *daśā*. Year 47, Month 4: Great gain of wealth. Year 48, Month 5: Great suffering from disease and loss of wealth. Year 49, Month 4: Suffering from the provocation of the three humors (*tridhātu*). Year 50: Fame, majesty, wealth, water, and happiness. Year 51, Month 5:

Gain of happiness; Year 52, Month 3: causing knowledge. Year 53, Month 4: fondness for strife. Year 54, Month 4: gain of the meaning of knowledge. Year 55, Month 7: evil period (kudaśā). Year 56, Month 8: auspicious. Year 57, Month 9: family conflict. Year 59: auspicious. Year 60: period of defects (cchidradaśā); [this is] the maximum lifespan.
He lives for eighty years, eighty years.
The results of the Vidha-dashas are completed.
He states the results of Ketu’s own period: Maghā, Mūlā, and Aśvinī. Year 0, month 9: suffering from fever and skin disease.

Year 1, month 7: acquisition of gold, clothing, and other goods. Year 2, month 4: danger of fever and dysentery. Year 3, month 2: gain of wealth and prosperity. Year 3, month 11: danger from falling objects, fire, and the disease of boils.

Year 4, month 8: untimely death. Year 5, month 6: attainment of all goals. Year 6, month 5: sorrow and fear. Year 7: middling. Year 8: auspicious. Year 9, month 4: middling. Year 10: auspicious. Year 11, month 6: loss of wealth. Year 12: gain of a wife. Year 13: middling. Year 14, month 9: mixed results.

Year 15: Mid-year. Year 16, month 11: Fear from weapons, fire, poison, and snakes. Year 18: Fear of the king. Year 19, month 1: Misfortune caused by women. Year 21, month 4: Attainment of a son and acquisition of royal favor. Year 22: Suffering and fear of the king. Year 23, month 7: Distress and loss of wealth. Year 24: Auspicious. Year 25.
In the ninth month, various gains (p.
76b). In the fourteenth year, fear of separation from kinsmen. In the fifteenth year and first month, suffering from illness. In the sixteenth year, auspiciousness.

Year 17, month 7: anger arises in three ways. Year 19: auspicious. Year 20: an evil period (kudaśā). Year 20, month 8: suffering from the king. Year 21, month 4: gain of women, clothing, food, and vehicles. Year 22: fear of fever, pain, and dysentery. Year 22, month 8: fear of falling from a height, fire, and weapons. Year 23, month 4: great profit. Year 24.

Suffering from lodging [24th year, 8 months]; gain [25th year, 8 months]; loss of a son [26th year]; gain of wealth through effort [27th year, 2 months]; gain of auspicious wealth [28th year, 3 months];
great fear and conflict [29th year]; a period of obstacles [30th year, 6 months]; attainment of desires [31st year].

In the 31st year, 7 months: suffering from imprisonment and bodily pain. In the 32nd year, 8 months: auspicious. In the 33rd year, 9 months: causing loss of sons and wealth. In the 34th year, 11 months: auspicious; attainment of learning and prosperity. In the 36th year: danger from fever, enemies, and enmity with kinsmen.

Year 37, month 6: Kudaśā (minor period). Year 38, month 6: Royal honors. Year 39, month 11: Various sufferings. Year 40, month 7: Fear of weapons and thieves. Year 41, month 4: Fear of fire. Year 42: Auspicious. Year 43: Loss of wealth and grief caused by women. Year 44: Supreme affliction. Year 45: [Auspicious].
The year 46 brings auspiciousness and the fulfillment of all goals; the year 47 brings fear of weapons; the year 48 is a period of vulnerability.

The forty-ninth year is middling; the fiftieth year brings gain; the fifty-first year is auspicious; the fifty-second year brings loss of one's desired objects through anxiety; the fifty-third year brings auspicious gain; the fifty-fourth year is auspicious; the fifty-fifth year brings great fear; the fifty-sixth year is middling; the fifty-seventh year brings gain; the fifty-ninth year is a period of ill fortune (kudaśā); the sixtieth year is a period of vulnerability and constraint (cchidrasaṃvada-daśā), during which one must be cautious lest death occur.
The maximum lifespan is seventy-two years; one lives for seventy-two years. Thus ends the results of Venus's own period.
(p. 78b) Now he states the results for the first ascendant: [one who is] intensely angry, fond of traveling to foreign lands, and greedy.
A body with hard skin; a state of little happiness; possessed of envy; behaving improperly; and a body afflicted by wind, bile, fever, and pain.
Skilled in action; one whose head is bowed with fear; eyes resembling gold; lover of the Dharma; one whose intellect is as vast as the earth.
He causes the loss of others' wealth; he is timid; he is unsuccessful; he has a dejected countenance; he is without kinsmen; and he is unpleasant to his father.
Swift-moving; having few sons; endowed with various forests and so forth; of beautiful character.
Birth in a contemptible family; suffering for one's own self; causing hatred among kinsmen; and obtaining a wife.
In the first stage of life, one who is dull-witted and happy through unwholesome actions attains the fruit of being bound by a girdle. 1.

Capable; dear to his father and mother; enduring hardships; fearless; a slayer of enemies; habituated to accumulating wealth during his youth; firm-hearted; accomplishing tasks through diligence; illustrious; and generous by nature.
One who causes the expenditure of various kinds of wealth.
Extremely brilliant; having a constitution of wind and phlegm (*vāta-śleṣma*); father of two daughters and one son; hating his own kinsmen; devoid of steadfastness.

Devoid of wealth, dear to wicked people, fickle, fond of food, addicted to drink, addicted to perfumes, and possessing many kinds of garments and ornaments—such is the result of the Taurus ascendant (2). One who is clever in conversation with women and of a generous disposition.
Proud, possessing excellent speech; having himself as his mother and fire as his maternal uncle; a youth; not knowing [the ways of] men; fond of dance and song.

One who performs the highest rites; one who knows the Vedas and grammar; one whose smile is steady; one fond of poetry; one who is peaceful; one fond of ornaments; one whose character is passionate; one fond of social gatherings; one who is impatient; one who has unpleasant sons; and one who is lacking in intelligence.
Trembling, deficient in limbs, having extra feet, slow in action, with protruding eyes, and thick eyelids.
O destroyer of the hosts of fierce enemies! O bestower of the earth, fire, and gold! O you who are endowed with pearls and other such jewels!

The results for Gemini Ascendant (Mithuna-lagna): || 3 || Fearful by nature; does not remain in one place; clever; of an intelligent disposition; deceitful; extremely sickly; and becomes an object of enmity. || 1 || (From page 79b, the results for the first sign-ascendant are stated: Skilled; of a wise character; free from deceit; and exceedingly ill. He becomes an enemy to his kinsmen. || 2 ||
Greedy for great fires; not devoted to Brahmins and gods; having an intellect for dharma; afflicted with phlegmatic disease; greedy for women.
Skilled in constant lamentation, the younger brother of his sister, deprived of kinsmen, and even the meagerness of a bad son.

One who speaks ill of his kinsmen, one whose three supports (parents and wife) are censured, one who enjoys the wealth of others, a debtor, a resident of a foreign land, a powerful lord, one who performs no religious rites, and one who praises himself—all such things [occur]; yet he is happy with the enjoyment of ornaments and his wife. This is the result of the Cancer ascendant. 4. One fond of meat, one who incurs the anger of kings and suffers loss of wealth, and one devoid of righteousness.
He does not dwell in one place; he abandons his kinsmen and wives; he has a face like a lion; and his complexion is steady.
He possesses an extraordinary and excellent youth; he is radiant; he speaks very little; he is greedy and hostile toward others; and he is hungry.
One who sports in the mountain forests; one whose anger is momentary and whose friendship is firm; one who does not harm a friend even for a slight fault; and one who is difficult to look upon.
The one who causes the enemy to flee.
One who is devoted to his famous son, auspicious, wealthy through agriculture and trade, and fond of his wife.

The results of the Leo ascendant: It causes the loss of much wealth; [one becomes] a lute-player or a woman; [one is] under the control of others; [one is] subject to women; [one is] a tooth-merchant. This is the result of the Leo ascendant.
5 || One of graceful speech; one who knows the treatises on logic; one who is fond of cold [or: disciplined]; one who knows the highest actions; one who knows the treatises on poetry.
One who possesses many captivating stories, is not overly talkative, delights in giving, is fond of food, and is capable of sexual pleasure.
Stable-minded, compassionate, one who enjoys the wealth of others, prone to wandering, possessing the nature of a woman, and knowing the seasons.
A rogue, one whose nature is to adorn, powerful, handsome, lustful, a partaker of fame, and exceedingly righteous.
Virtuous, pure by nature and form, devoted to the gods, yet devoid of the conduct befitting his own caste, he was even hated by his brothers.
The son-producing [planet], wind-disease, dull-witted person, birth of an enemy, the art of storytelling, the results of the Virgo ascendant (kanyālagna), 6;
deformed body, devoid of ethics, fickle, slow in action, and causing the loss of wealth.
One with a dark body, fallen from one's own country, having a constitution of wind and phlegm, fond of mountain caves, and a deity of the upper body.
Exceedingly virtuous in character, knower of justice, enjoyer of pleasures, eloquent in speech, slayer of enemies, auspicious Kṛṣṇa, and the eye.
Devoted to guests, Brahmins, and the gods; learned; diligent in action; a servant of his guru; honorable; and possessing sons born of others.
One who hates the wise; one who is fierce; an enemy; one who acts according to [his] younger brother; one who possesses wealth; one who is pure.
One who harbors sinful thoughts toward her brother or brother-in-law; one devoted to other men; and one who is unrighteous—these are to be avoided as gains.
The results for the Ascendant (Lagna): [One] with a body that is stout, broad, and long; prone to anger; having weak digestion; and heroic.

One who does not consume food; one with the color of thick gold; one with large eyes; one with long arms; one with a deep belly; one with a nose like that of a horse; one who is free from disease; one who possesses stability; one who is fierce; and one who protects the wealth of others.
One who carries off his son; one afflicted by diseases of wind and phlegm; one who has many kinsmen; one who hates his guru; and one who delights in hating his friends.
He plays by means of force with another man's wife.
One who speaks with quarrelsome harshness; a servant of a king; one who delights in enmity; a giver to servants; and one who covets another's wife.

One who increases in righteousness, compassionate, diligent, [like] fruit clinging to a tree; one with abundant food, a long and thick head, a doer of what is dear to servants, endowed with fortitude and strength, yet fearful, dark-blue, and having a crooked nose.

The sixteen known as the vowels are established in the vyāna-cakra;
however, two are situated in the vyoma-cakra, having the nature of the *haṃsa* and the vital breath (*prāṇa*).
The letter *ha* is known as the vital breath (*prāṇa*), while the letter *sa* is called the downward breath (*apāna*).
The knot of these two, the *prāṇa* and *apāna*, is situated at the point of entry and exit.
That wheel, filled with the individual soul (jīva), is situated within all bodies;
it is celebrated as having six spokes, by which, O Goddess, bondage is produced.
The support of the stages, situated in the apāna and known as the sun, is pierced by the prāṇa-cakra;

As long as there is connection with the six chakras, so long is one said to be in saṃsāra;
