A man born on the new moon day (Amāvāsyā) will be steadfast in his undertakings, hostile to enemies, eloquent in speech, valorous, a secret friend, and endowed with wisdom.
Now, the results for the days of the week.
A man born on a Tuesday dominated by bile (pitta) is a consumer of sweet foods, prone to anger, fond of pleasure, and desirous of wealth.
Men who are enjoyers of pleasures, seekers of desire, knowers of the scriptures, and proud of their virtues. || 2 ||
A man who is exceedingly thin, parched, and burnt, yet possesses a clever nature, and who is a consumer of sweet food and drink, is born under the constellation Jyeṣṭhā. || 3 ||
A man born in Āṣāḍha becomes free from the four diseases, very handsome, endowed with intelligence, free from illness, and wealthy.
He has the form of a physician's staff and is enveloped in the skin of a black antelope.
If a man who knows the Dharma becomes a donor, he is born as a Śrāvaka.
A man who is knowledgeable in the scriptures, free from inauspiciousness, devoid of greed, and devoted to charity, meditation, and austerity,
is surely born when the month of Bhādrapada occurs.
A man born in Ākhāḍha becomes happy, beloved, learned in the Vedas, honored by kings, an acquirer of wealth, truthful in speech, and one who brings happiness to his servants. (7)

A man born in the month of Kārttika becomes one who possesses a great body and other [fine] qualities, is worthy of worship by the gods, a lord of wealth, and always endowed with diverse intelligence. (8)
Possessing great wisdom and great enjoyment, a knower of the Dharma and beloved by people, honored by the gods, he purifies the eightfold human states through great knowledge. || 1 ||
In the eleventh month, there is an eclipse of the moon;
in the sixteenth [month], and at twenty-seven years, death occurs on the fourth day of the dark fortnight.
In the thirty-second year, there will be a second affliction of the head during the period of Mars;
he shall live for seventy-four years, though constantly afflicted by disease. (3)
In the eighth month of the year of Mercury, there will be suffering, and in the eighth year thereafter,
at the completion of sixty-four years, death is proclaimed to occur.
If [the Moon] is in the seventh house from Jupiter in the seventh month, or in the thirteenth house in the sixteenth month, there is suffering; thereafter, one lives for eighty years.
On Friday, he will be free from diseases of his wife's body;
that man will certainly live for a full sixty years.
In the first month of Śanaiścara [Dasa], there are eighteen years of affliction;
however, if his body remains firm at that time, he lives for a hundred years.
Now, the results of the planetary groups (gaṇas).
One who is always of a very generous nature and possesses wisdom, yet is devoid of strength, becomes a person of meager enjoyments. (4)

A man born under the fifth [sign] becomes a practitioner of worldly affairs, one who accepts what is offered by his elders, a protector of his father and others, a donor, an enjoyer, and one who finds pleasure in his own body.
A man born on the sixth lunar day (Ṣaṣṭhī) becomes one who travels to various countries, is always prone to quarreling, and is constantly afflicted by digestive disorders.
A man born on the seventh lunar day becomes one who possesses few enemies, is radiant, beautiful with the quality of good fortune, endowed with sons, and possessed of wealth.
On the eighth day, a man is born who is righteous, truthful, a giver, an enjoyer, patient, and a knower of virtues in all undertakings.
A man who gives to the gods, has sons, possesses wealth, and whose mind is immersed in women, who is always devoted to his wife and not to others, becomes a Navamī-born man.
On the tenth [tithi], the man becomes a knower of dharma and non-dharma, a server of the gods, a purifier, rich in virtues, a knower of the Vedas, and one who conquers the wise and the brahmins.
In the year Varṣākāra, a man will become a long-time resident of the house of a non-royal lord;

he will be a knower of Dharma, discerning, skilled in serving his teacher, and an eloquent debater. Furthermore, he will engage in trade and agriculture and possess an abundance of wealth and grain. (p. 95a)
And a man becomes radiant and full of self-respect when autumn arrives. || 5 ||
Possessing great vigor, endowed with fierce brilliance, always eating first,
having short legs and a large body, and being fearful— such a man is born in the winter season.
Now follows the determination according to the stages (bhūmi).
The Agni Purāṇa and Varāhamihira.
The illustrious Lord said:
I shall now describe the mandalas characterized by the four unmanifested [elements]:
Kṛttikā, Maghā, Puṣya, and Pūrvaphalgunī.
Viśākhā, Bharaṇī, and likewise Pūrvabhādrapadā constitute the Āgneya-maṇḍala; I shall now describe its characteristics.
If the wind blows violently here, or if there is an eclipse of the moon and the sun, or an earthquake, or a thunderclap, or an eclipse of the moon and the sun;
One born on a Monday will have smoke and flames as omens, suffer from burning sensations, and possess uncontrolled senses; yet he becomes preeminent in learning and endowed with virtuous conduct. (2)
A man [ruled] by Mars becomes fond of fools, wealthy, cruel, a reviler of the Vedas and the Smṛtis, devoid of faith, godless, and diseased.
On the day of Wednesday, one is born endowed with the performance of Vedic scriptures and rituals, becomes highly learned,
and is engaged in terrifying and formidable activities.
He will be wealthy, possessing great wealth and a sword, with a prominent knee and many servants; he may also be born on a Thursday, a Sunday, or a Monday. || 5 ||
On a Thursday, a person becomes a knower of the Vedas, a performer of the Agnihotra sacrifice, endowed with sons, grandsons, and wealth,
possessed of progeny, and full of mental clarity.
On the day of Īśa (Monday), one is born base, powerless, ungrateful, crooked, a tormentor of kinsmen, a destroyer of accomplished tasks, and wrathful.
Or else, it is the afterbirth.

In the first month of misfortune, in the thirty-second, the thirteenth, and also in the sixth, one born under the Sun moves about alive; however, if some disorder should arise, one should know that it extends to the region of Mahendra. I shall describe its characteristics.
All the subjects will be delighted, and all fierce [calamities] will be avoided in that [kingdom];
the kings will form alliances, and there will be abundance of food for the ruler.
Samūdra, Āmagadha, and likewise Madhyadeśa;
the entire Kurukṣetra and also Pāṇipathya.
If they perish in that place, it is due to the sight of the small boat.
Ārdrā, Śatabhiṣā, Āśleṣā, Pūrvāṣāḍhā, Revatī, Mūlā, and likewise Uttarabhādrapadā— these are the seven constellations of the field (kṣetra).

If there is any movement here, or if some transformation should occur, one should recognize it as extending to the end of the Varuṇa region; I shall describe its characteristics: cows will yield much milk and ghee, and women will likewise have sons.
The rivers will increase in depth, and the earth will abound with many crops.
One should predict good harvests, security, and health for all living beings.
The Vindhya mountains and the central region (Madhyadeśa), as well as the lands of the Brahmins and Kṣatriyas, will flourish.
One who desires the kingdom and possesses great wisdom shall become a leader among the hosts of men and gods. || 1 ||

In the Mānavega class [of men], one is born who is proud, wealthy, with piercing eyes, a marksman capable of hitting a target at a distance of a hundred thousand [leagues], a wielder of the bow, and a delight to the cowherds and the common people. (2)
One who possesses a terrifying appearance, is intoxicated, and is fond of the company of all people, becomes a Pramehin and is born among the hosts of Rākṣasas. || 3 ||
Now, the fruit of the seasons.
A man born under Śiśira is endowed with beauty and long life, but is intoxicated by pride, afflicted by hunger, and lustful. (1)
In the spring, a man becomes intoxicated with vigor, free from lethargy, radiant, a performer of many deeds, and well-acquainted with various countries. || 2 ||
Anger is his necklace; he is hungry, yet a consumer of food; he is a man of desire; he is long, yet composed and free from pride; born in the summer, he is ever pure. || 3 ||
He will be virtuous, possessed of enjoyments, honored by kings, with subdued senses,
and likewise like a deer.
All are tormented by disease, and others likewise take away their lives.
Their own abodes perish in villages and cities;
these regions are destroyed—such is the characteristic omen of that portent.
The Āgneya lasts for three months, the Vāruṇa for two months,
the Vāyavya for one month, and the Māhendra for seven nights.
One should designate the Āgneya year as one with much rain, the Vāruṇa as having abundant rain,
the Vāyavya as free from disease, and the Māhendra as drought.
1. Oṃ, homage to the glorious Mṛtyuñjaya!
"O Lord, tell me clearly how these portents have arisen;
O Great Lord, I bow to you, for an excessive trembling has occurred throughout the quarters."
The illustrious Lord said:
Listen, O Goddess, I shall explain [this method] for examining the auspicious and inauspicious;
this has been spoken falsely for the sake of the welfare of human beings.
Having entered the forest of black tigers, one does not die for three years.
May there be peace for him.
The torment caused by the performance of the great *bali* offering.
The rising of comets and likewise the falling of stars;
Where there is a rain of blood, a rain of animals, and likewise the falling of stones;
where calamities arise and reservoirs of water dry up.
And if at this time some disorder should arise,
there may be eye disease, diarrhea, and the digestive fire becomes sluggish.
Cows yielding little milk and ghee, trees bearing few flowers and fruits, and the destruction of crops— these indicate that one should predict scant rainfall.
Men are seen with skulls in their hands, being tormented by the king of men.
The people of the four castes were tormented by hunger, being afflicted and miserable.
The Saindhavas, Āyamuṇas, Kāmbojas, and Vāhlikas,
as well as Jālandhara, Kāśmīra, Nepāla, and Uttarāpatha.
These regions perish upon the appearance of that portent. || 1 ||
Jyeṣṭhā, Rohiṇī, Anurādhā, Śravaṇa, Dhaniṣṭhā, Uttarāṣāḍhā, and Abhijit as the seventh; thus [are the seven].
Wherever there is worship of the field and the deity, the feeding of the fivefold assembly of Brahmins with nectar-like food, and the giving of a sacrificial fee according to one's capacity; || 5 ||

Having overcome internal strife or even death to one's master within ten months, his pacification occurs at dawn through the worship of a water-pot (*kalaśa*). Having fashioned an image out of silver, it should be given to a Brahmin, along with food and ghee for the crows. || 6 ||
By the entry of a snake into the house, the death of the master occurs within six months, or else there is a great loss of wealth.

For his pacification, one should perform an oblation at dawn using sesame, the three fruits (*triphalā*), the three sweets (*trimadhu*), *śrībhokā* wood, and eight types of sacrificial fuel (*samidh*).
One should offer oblations consisting of the five limbs [of the plant], combined with seven grains, ghee, sesame, and unbroken rice (*akṣata*).
There are two water-pots (*kalaśa*), eight offerings (*bali*), thirty-four food-offerings (*naivedya*), one *khāla*, thirty-four *myālanaivedya*, and meat equal to me.

If, after removing earth from a place where liquor, milk, or the entry of scorpions and snakes has occurred, one offers it as a water-oblation (*udakabali*) in a place of impurity, there will be defeat for those who have come for victory in battle;
a terrible war will break out between rival kings. (3)
Hasta, Citrā, as well as Svāti, Mṛgaśīrṣa, Punarvasu,
Uttaraphalgunī, and Aśvinī is the seventh.
If anything should move here, or if any modification should occur;
One should know it to extend as far as the northwest; I shall describe its characteristics.
Famine, pestilence among people, and a rain of stones upon the earth.
And though they appear most terrible, no milk or venom is found within them.
Walls, gateways, and other structures are established upon the surface of the earth;
likewise, there are variegated trees of great size and divine abodes.
Driven by the force of the wind, they all fall to the ground;
likewise, both men and women are tormented by hunger.

The kings of Kāmboja, Uśīnara, Kukkura, Vāhlīka, and likewise the Aṅga country, as well as those of Madhyadeśa, will wage war against one another. Elephants, horses, and men— [the lands of] Ṣara, Uhārṇu, Āḍharūṣa, Sinduvāri, and Apāmārga.

One should offer oblations with these: *priyaṅgu*, *savoḍiṃ*, *hāsuva*, honey, and sour *durvā* grass. A gift of fine cloth, gold, and a golden image of a man should be given, followed by the feeding of five Brahmins. || 10 ||
If a fish is swallowed by a crocodile out of nowhere, there will be the destruction of one's master and the loss of wealth within three years.
For its pacification, three measures of grain made of gold by Hiraṇyagarbha should be given, and one should provide a meal.
If there is fruit and flowers out of season, or the appearance of new rain-clouds, there will be no death for the master, but rather separation from his wife;
the pacification of this [is as follows].
The gift of a vessel of molasses and the feeding of Brahmins. || 12 ||
If [the moon] is afflicted by Svāti, Anurādhā, Pādā (Punarvasu), Aṅgāraka (Mṛgaśīrṣa), or Mūla, there is disease or loss of wealth; if afflicted by Viṣṭi, there is the death of a son;
and by the purification of Viṣṭi, there is disease and grief for three years. The pacification of this is as follows.

Having fashioned an image of Svānasya (the Dog-faced One) from *vali* offerings, the wise man, intent on worship, should give a gift of one measure of husked rice according to the *mṛtyuñjaya* rite. (p. 99b)
Cows, gold, and Brahmins who have reached the further shore of the Vedas should be given as gifts;
one should feed the Brahmins with milk and clarified butter, for thus peace is attained.
In the same way, the fruit is released through a violent upheaval during the day;
likewise, the rite of pacification (śānti) should be performed. || 2 ||
In the event of a rainbow appearing at night or a lightning strike, peace should be performed in exactly the same manner as for the attainment of the fruit. || 3 ||
If a well-pole is obtained, the master will die at the end of four years.

The pacification of that [evil influence] consists of offerings of water-born flowers, silver, and a well, as well as worship of the Naga; at the conclusion of the meal of milk and clarified butter, a gold gift should be given according to one's capacity. || 4 ||
With hair and beard shorn, dwelling in a cremation ground, he was one who had renounced worldly life.
There is danger from fire for four years; its pacification [is achieved] as follows:

ten days prior [to the onset], one should not perform [the usual rites]; ten *raktikās* of silver should be given to a Brahmin; at night, there should be the offering of the seasonal oblation (*samayabali*) and worship. || 16 ||
If a mountain collapses, there will be an earthquake, famine, or the destruction of the ruler;
through rain, there is peace for that [region].
The gift of cattle, land, and gold, as well as a *śānti-homa* performed at the site of the collapsed mountain, brings peace. (17)

If one's own shadow or the head is not seen, or if the shadow of the house and so forth is not seen, death or exile will occur within three years; its pacification is as follows: a copper vessel filled with sesame seeds should be offered while placed upon Hiranyagarbha, and one should perform the worship of the water-pot (kalaśa), offer a bali-oblation to Kṣetrapāla, and provide a meal. || 18 ||

If there is the appearance of flowers and excessive fruit, there will be the loss of one's wife and the depletion of wealth; for that, pacification by means of the left side of a goat and white thread is required.
The worship of the Tīrtha-vessel, the offering of the site-oblation (sthānavali), and the giving of a sacrificial fee (dakṣiṇā) according to one's capacity. || 19 ||

If it is impossible [to perform the rite] at the site, it may be done in the house; for one who has obtained water, the pacification of the destruction of the site, the movement from the site, or the house occurs through the application of half of that [same measure].

The gift of a white wick and a cow, the gift of a kumārī along with her husband, a bronze vessel containing the reflection of the moon and filled with the three sweets placed within it, a sacrificial fee (dakṣiṇā), and the feeding of Brāhmaṇas. || 7 ||

If there is a garland of musk-shrews, or exhaustion and separation from one's wife, one should perform a pacification rite by means of oblations, or the gift of gold, or the feeding of the poor, and the worship of Vināyaka. (8)
If an unprecedented death of a living being occurs in the outer courtyard or within the house, it is declared by the wise master to be the *Varṣa* [year] of Catura.

For its pacification, one should perform a fire-oblation (*homa*), give a gift of a metal vessel filled with honey, and provide food together with the installation of the *Hiraṇyagarbha* [image]. || 9 ||

If the parasol or banner of Maināka falls, there will be great fear from the fire of hungry ghosts (*preta*) and danger to the kingdom; or due to great pestilences (*mārimahāmāri*), there will be loss of wealth. Within seven years, there is no peace for him. Having gone to a river at dawn to bathe, he should perform a fire-oblation (*homa*) at the appropriate sacred site (*kramasthāna*).
Lāhacūrṇa, āḍharūṣa, *sundhuvāri*, apārga, *priyaṅgu*, *vaṃvodiṃti*, a vessel of sesame seeds, or a golden *tilaka* [are the offerings]. || 23 ||
p. 101a) When a deity’s vessel or water-pot suddenly falls during a divine consecration (*devādhiṣṭhāna*), it portends the death of the patron within one year;
the pacification (*śānti*) for this is as follows:
one should offer oblations (*juhuyāt*) by mixing powdered *madhuka*, iron filings, red sesame seeds, and seven types of grain with mustard oil (*kaṭutaila*).
One should offer as food ghee mixed with milk-rice and a red goat; [the gift] includes a cow, gold, a silver vessel, and an image made of gold. || 24 ||

If the goddess Mahiṣādi is worshipped at the time of ritual with an offering devoid of red color and appearing discolored, there will be the death of her husband within one year; for its pacification, the cutting off of enjoyments must be performed, and the five-fold offering (pañcopahāra) along with meat must be given as food. || 25 ||
If an elephant, horse, buffalo, goat, or similar animal dies suddenly, even though its owner is not present, it is said that its pacification occurs within three years;
[the remedy is] the gift of a goat, the consecration [of an image], and gold. || 26 ||
O dear one, whether in a garden or in a house, the field-guardian shall not give a vessel of molasses as a gift;
O Hiraṇyagarbha, sixteen great meals, accompanied by ten thousand established offerings, must be given with red [substances]. || 13 ||

If a vessel for food, a vessel for sour gruel, a vessel for curd, a vessel for water, a vessel for milk, or a vessel for liquor, or even fish, meat, or a solid mass [of food], falls or is broken, within seven years the death of the householder occurs.

For its pacification, one should perform bathing at a sacred ford (tīrtha), worship of the ritual pitcher (kalaśa), offering of oblations (bali) at the site, worship of the serpent (nāga), and the use of *damana* flowers, *śrīkhaṇḍa* sandalwood, and red sandalwood.
Gold, silver, elephants, and food should be given as gifts. 14.
If there is a sudden fall of a meteor, or if the master dies from a stroke of lightning, the pacification of that [evil influence] is through the gift of land or gold. 15.
If death is foretold for one year by observing a gap between the moon and the sun, its pacification is as follows:

a copper vessel (16 units) filled with cow’s ghee, containing gold, pearls, and an emerald, together with a water-pot for the rite of purification at sacred sites, along with sugar; this is the meal offering.
If water suddenly becomes clear, there will be the destruction of one's master within three years; if it overflows excessively, there will be loss of wealth for him.
To pacify this, one should go to a place where water has appeared as an omen, perform rites involving aquatic creatures, give gifts of gold, and honor the Brahmins.

After honoring the guests with hospitality, they partook of a meal prepared according to their respective rites, served in vessels of ghee, and accompanied by the performance of worship at its conclusion. || 28 ||

If [the affliction] has been sown in the field or seed, or if it arises from other substances, it is not born [as a simple ailment], but rather within twelve months there occurs a great disease involving a threat to life.
Its pacification is through the gift of a sword (*kṣatra*), or an offering of five swords, accompanied by worship including non-violence (*ahiṃsā*) and the goddess Kaumārī.
It should be given within the circle of the pledge (samayacakra). || 29 ||

If the crow alights on its own body, there is the attainment of two things; if it alights on the daughter, death; if on the arm, a great disease; if on the two hips, suffering from the king; if on the stone, loss of wealth and food. || 20 ||
Suddenly, by the collapse of the palace, after four years.
There is peace for him.

Having offered oblations with this six-syllable mantra using barley, unbroken rice, sesame, mustard, *śamī*, *ekaṅkana*, *palaṣa*, *khadira*, *apāmārga*, *devadāru*, and the wood of *śrīśobha*, one should place two *śānti* jars and perform the *netra-vidhi* and the *bali* offering.
For the destruction of the site or location, having given an offering of earth according to this procedure— [The ritual for the destruction of the site or location is completed.]
That which must be offered at death:
gold for the gift, a sword sharpened for a month, three *prasthas* of black-pleasing black beans, a vessel of molasses, and the portion for Kaumārī. || 21 ||
For one who has attained a crown in the house, there shall be no great disease for one year;
its pacification [is achieved] by offering a copper vessel filled with milk along with a crown, a golden egg (hiraṇyagarbha), a white cloth, a covering, and a meal of milk. || 22 ||

If there is a sudden fall of the body, death will not occur in the eighth month; however, there will be the destruction of his wife and children, loss of half his wealth, and death after [that period]. For the pacification of these signs of *kālataka* (the black messenger of death), one should perform the following rite: having performed the morning bath, worship the water-pot (*kalaśa*) at home, offer the *sthānavali*, and place an egg upon a black cloth.
One should not make a banner; [there should be] thirty (30) water-offerings (*udakabali*) and two (2) vessel-offerings (*pātranivedya*).

One should cause a water-offering to be given at the wooden beam of a crow's nest. At the place where the house was built, one should wash with milk; one should not clean it with the five products of the cow (*pañcagavya*). Incense, *japamāṃsī*, *uśīra*, *kastūrī*, and *guggulu*—these are now offered.
Gold for the gift, a consecrated white cloth, silver— not [merely] its own form— having fashioned a copper vessel with three pieces of meat;
together with a meal accompanied by the consecration of a golden embryo filled with jaggery, this should be given to a Brahmin who knows the *trimadhu*.
Together. || 31 ||

If a crow scratches its own body, that very [act] results in the destruction of the master who has not yet received the fruit of the peace-offering jar (śāntidānakalaśa) worship; [this occurs] by means of two dogs. His pacification [is as follows]: p. 103b) His pacification:

One should perform the fire-oblation (homa) for the gift-cloth together with the consecration (pratiṣṭhā), but not the worship of the water-jar (kalaśa-arcana), nor the offering of oblations (bali-pradāna). At the site of the field (kṣetra-sthāna), there is the worship of the Yoginīs, Vaṭuka, and Gaṇapati, along with the offering of oblations and food-offerings (naivedya); this constitutes thirty-five [items].
There is one black cloth for the banner (patākā) and one black rag (karpatam), two wicks (varti), and eight pieces of auspicious wood (śrīsobhakāṣṭha).
One should offer oblations of aśvattha, udumbara, and vaikaṅkata wood, along with triphalā and the three sweets (trimadhu).

Having removed the earth from the site of entry, one should cause a water-offering (udakabali) to be given. After that, having offered sesame seeds, rice, and so forth, as well as a snake-oblation, one should face the east or another direction; immediately thereafter, [one should perform] the gift of the *tāmlapra* and the *tilayapūlita* Hiraṇyagarbha.
Covered with a red cloth, there is the recitation of the *Śāntika* chapter and so forth according to one's own ritual procedure;
the offering of a golden vessel for the sun’s station, the installation (*pratiṣṭhā*), a vessel of moon-essence rays, the three sweets (*trimadhu*),
and within the interval between the two, a sword that trembles, free from sorrow, not joined by the tip of the year’s rain.
There is peace for him.
At night, there shall be worship of Durgā, the offering of oblations, and the gift of a sword together with meat; [this is] the worship of Kaumārī and the gold dakṣiṇā. || 35 ||
If a crow builds its nest in a temple, a vacant site, or a house, there will be no fear of foreign armies, but there will be local unrest, fire, and destruction.
If it does so in the eastern direction, death occurs; in the west, conflict; in the south-west, grief;
in the south-east, suffering; in the north, loss; in the north-east, ruin; in the south, people are oppressed; and in the south-west, defeat.
O kings, death on the ground is certain;
however, in a conflict arising from the command of a spy or a secret agent,
one should not engage in war with one's own army or the enemy's army within the country.
In the place of the temple of Śāntideva, at the site of worship and the area for the *bali* offering, there is a great *bali* and a copper vessel filled with sesame seeds and salt.
Death will occur by being struck on the head within three months; there is fear of rain and enemies, and grief regarding women in the stomach and mouth for one year.
Peace, bathing for a long time, offerings and worship at the time of night, the timely offering, the gift of copper vessels for food, a bell-metal vessel, and the sacrificial fee (dakṣiṇā). || 30 ||

If a crow builds its nest within the interior of a house, there is danger from fire for one year. If it builds a large nest on a roof-awning (*chānikā*), there will be the entry of a dark man (*kālapuruṣa*) who is constantly present in the assembly. If it builds its nest in the place of *kailāśa*, there is grief concerning the wife and others due to the house itself. By the falling of a crow into a well, the master will be imprisoned within a month or at the end of the year.
If at the time of eating one is touched by a crow, there will be fear of the king, or exile, or confinement.

If a dog enters the house from the east, there will be grief caused by the destruction of the household; from the south, death; from the west, loss; from the north, disease; from the southeast, death; from the southwest, loss of wealth; and from the northwest, loss. If a human hand, foot, or piece of flesh ever reaches the house, the master’s death will occur within four years.

For his pacification, one should perform the *mṛtyuñjaya-vidhāna* (the rite for conquering death). One should offer oblations into the fire; [one should give] a vessel filled with milk, accompanied by the orb of the moon, containing pearls, gold, and a recitation as a sacrificial fee (*dakṣiṇā*).
Whether in a temple or in a village, through the entry of forest-dwelling birds and the like during the bright fortnight, [this shall be accomplished] within three years.

For one who considers himself a master, there is peace through the worship of the water-pot (kalaśa) in the home, the giving of the three great garlands, and the propitiation of the Yoginīs of the field and Vaṭuka.

For the installation and drawing forth [of the deity], there should be a vessel filled with the ghee of the gift-cow, containing coral within, together with gold as a sacrificial fee and edible offerings. || 39 ||
By the time of death born of the six-month period, the father met his destruction within nine years.

The worship of the peace-vase (śāntikalaśa), the worship of the sacrificial offering (bali), the gift of a copper vessel (tāmrapātra) filled with cow’s milk and gold—these five [items] for the consecration (pratiṣṭhā). One should cause the offering at one's own place (svasthānabali) together with eight hundred eggs to be given. The worship of the Nāgas (nāgapūjā), the gift of a copper vessel (tāmrapātra) containing the three sweets (trimadhu), powdered [substances], and the lunar disc (candraviṃva)—these three [items] for the consecration and the meal. || 32 ||

In one's own villages, there shall be the destruction of the kingdom by a person born under the Aṇu asterism and the suffering of the subjects; due to a piece of wood brought by a crow from near the water—brought by a minor individual—the kingdom will be destroyed as if in a forest. Its pacification occurs through the performance of a great bali-offering. || 33 ||
For a man born under Jamala-jātaka, there will be deep drinking of wine by buffaloes or by horses; he will lose his family and his master will perish due to rain.
His pacification is as follows.

Having gone to a sacred ford (tīrtha), one should perform oblations, worship of the water-pot (kalaśa), and the installation of a banner; [the fee consists of] ten raktikās of gold, one banner, and food for a hundred people. || 34 ||
At the time of the sword-worship, by the falling of the sword, death occurs within three years; having become a buffalo, one reaches the abode of Yama, the Lord, after three years.
(106) The gift of a peace-buffalo or the gift of gold. || 44 ||
If the presiding deity of a location trembles, weeps, laughs, perspires, shakes, blazes, smokes, or sheds blood,
there will be the destruction of the kingdom and the ruin of the king within one year.

Śānti, that very same [rite] is the worship of the deity with a great offering (mahābali) together with the attendants; [likewise] for Kaumārī, there is the worship of the wheel (cakrapūjana). || 45 ||
In the temple, a necklace and earrings were stolen; by whom was this binding obtained? Thus [he asked] for a year.
Peace, according to one's ability, gold, the gift of a cow, or otherwise non-violence, along with worship, the offering of oblations, and food accompanied by meat. || 46 ||
If a house or temple is struck by a thunderbolt (*iṇḍibha*) or a *mukuti* [meteor/impact] more than once, the destruction of the master occurs within one year.
At the conclusion of the propitiatory rite (*śānti*), one should perform the gift of a cow, the gift of food, the gift of rags (*karpaṭa*), gold, a banner, and silver.

Having fashioned the form of a house-crow, one should offer a rag, gold, two jars, water from the *taśru* [river], two mustard seeds, the five products of the cow (*pañcagavya*), and a lamp. With salt, one should create a likeness of one's own body;
using a sword made of *kuśa* grass, one should sever its head. With devotion, one's own body should be given to a Brahmin. [This is] the threshing-floor. 1.

One *aṇuja* (1), six *apakosala* (6), stability (*sthānavali*), six pills (*guṭikā*) (6), six portions of food (*bhaktipiṇḍa*) (6), one *svatasarya* (1), one *svatakarpaṭa* (1), four finger-breadths (*aṅguli*) in measure, eight *pradākā* (6)—these are the desired qualities.
One should offer the wood from a crow’s nest along with water, an oblation (*vali*), and rice (*vrīhi*); it should not be given in any other place.

By the entry of a copper serpent, there is the destruction of one's master within one year; [for this,] peace is achieved by offering a bronze vessel filled with milk along with a golden image of Nanda, accompanied by a gift of gold. || 37 ||
According to whose rule [he should act]. || 50 ||
If [the serpent] ascends upon the limbs of a man or woman, he or she lives for one year, though there may be a great loss of wealth;

or, if it is in the ascendant (*lagna*), there is a loss of wealth and grain. If it reaches the shanks, there is imprisonment; if on the thighs, fear of enemies; if on the belly, the loss of a son; if on the chest, separation from one's wife; and if on the neck, a fall from one's position.
Fear of kings shall depart from the mouth; the ears shall attain the arrival of fortune; one shall obtain the station of sovereignty.
For the pacification of inauspiciousness and ill-repute, one should perform oblations according to the *Mṛtyuñjaya* rite.
One should give as a gift to a worthy recipient seven measures of gold, along with a golden image of the Sun, and grain mixed with honey.
An installation should be performed, and food accompanied by gold and the three sweets (trimadhu) should be offered. || 51 ||

O Shadow-Person, by the sight of this falling [offering], may there be no entry of the Person of Time (Kālapuruṣa). For one year, through single-minded devotion, may there be the pacification of loss of wealth; may there be the pacification by the water-pot rite (udakakuṃbha-śānti); and may there be the pacification of birth (jāti-śānti) for the jars, the water-filled vessels, and the ladles. || 40 ||
At the time of dawn, by means of the *Aśvajāyate* rite and the single *sthānabhraṃsavarṣa*,

one should offer a sun-oblation (*sūryārgha*) consisting of a copper vessel filled with silver, rice, grain, and milk, together with a horse, at midday; [otherwise] there will be a loss of wealth within six months.
The gift for peace consists of a tawny cow, gold, and the consecration ceremony.

If a horse is born in the afternoon, there will be the destruction of its master; for that, peace must be performed within three months according to the procedure for the *Mṛtyuñjaya-śāntika* chapter, consisting of recitation, gifts, and [donations of] cattle, land, and gold on the day [of birth]. || 41 ||
In the month of Āṣāḍha, there is great misfortune for one born under the constellation Aśvinī.
The gift of a horse produced by Śāntisāta was a reflection of his purpose. 42.
If a lion is born under the Sun or Śravaṇa, there will be no destruction of the master; however, at the end of the year, a cow born under Śānti should be given to a Brahmin. || 43 ||
Like one bitten by a snake, or as if fallen into a well, or afflicted by a chronic cough, or seeing something red or green that is not his own—
having thus reached a state of grief and fallen into anxiety, within six months, he shall find peace through the following rites:

visiting holy fords (*tīrtha*), worship of the water-pot (*kalaśa-pūjā*), worship of the serpent (*nāga-pūjā*), giving gifts according to one's capacity, the consecration of gold, and twelve copper plates.
12. The food, together with vegetables. || 55 ||

For one afflicted by wind-disorders (*vāta-vāhimanuṣa*) and for the pacification of separation from a woman, the installation [of the deity] should be performed with a broken copper vessel filled with milk and honey; [the offering consists of] silver food, sweetmeats, and finally five betel-rolls.
It should be given together with a skull-bowl. || 56 ||
If stones and such enter the house, death or disease will occur within seven months; its pacification is as follows:

one should give ten *ratī* of gold, offer oblations of milk, rice, and clarified butter into the fire, and perform the installation and worship of the deity with milk and clarified butter for the purpose of feeding [the community]. || 47 ||
If one encounters the danger of death from snakes, wild beasts, or enemies, there will be death within four months for one who has attained life.
For his pacification, one should offer oblations to each respective deity while remaining vigilant;
one should also recite the *Śāntika* [mantra] while meditating.

To the reciters and others, one should give gifts of gold, a yellow garment, a copper vessel, three *prasthas* of red-eyed grain filled with pure gold, along with food accompanied by sacrificial fees (*dakṣiṇā*). || 48 ||
By raining drops of red [substance] upon the houses, death occurs; there is destruction within three years.

For the pacification [of this], a great offering (mahābali) of red rain should be performed: having removed the earth from the site, one should place the offering in the center and deposit it in the location of the *ara*; one should fill it with pure earth.

Having established the yakṣa-offering, the site-offering, the bhūta-offering, and the divine offering (divali) within the house in the form of gifts, there shall be the installation of gold and food. || 49 ||

If one obtains meat being cooked in the house, the previously mentioned result will become unstable; therefore, having observed this, one should offer curd-water (*takra*) to a Brāhmaṇa. One should draw a figure of a man on a copper vessel with *gorocanā* pigment, place it inside an earthenware jar, and deposit within it one handful of unbroken rice (*akṣata*), one handful of mustard seeds (*sarṣapa*), and three *ratīs* of gold.
One should conceal it in the place of the wheel. || 60 ||
For one who has fallen into the calamity of the *cetāṅga* [constellation], there is danger from death and disease for one year;

[to pacify this, perform] daily bathing, the recitation (*pāṭha*) of the *Mṛtyuñjaya*, devotion to one’s chosen deity (*iṣṭadevatā*), circumambulation and prostration one hundred and eight times around the *aśvattha* tree, and the gift of a *kuḍava* measure of cow-ghee along with a vessel of molten gold.
Having observed [the recipient], a sacrificial fee of gold should be given according to one's ability. || 61 ||

Death occurs through the collapse of the house; separation [from loved ones] for one year [results from this]. To pacify it, one should give a white-colored cow as a gift, along with ten *ratikās* of gold as a priestly fee (*dakṣiṇā*). One should worship Indra as the presiding deity and offer a propitiatory oblation (*śānti-bali*) into a river.
A silver vessel filled with grain should be established and covered with a golden cloth, and a feast for Brahmins should be provided. || 52 ||

Near the house or in the city, a tiger may appear, or a monkey may cause the destruction of the region. There will be loss through one's own kin or loss of wealth. For three years, [the following remedies are prescribed]: the offering of a *śāntikarpaṭa* (peace-cloth), the gift of gold as a priestly fee (*dakṣiṇā*), the offering of oblations (*bali*), the performance of fire-sacrifices (*homa*) for pacification, the worship of the ritual water-pot (*kalaśa*), and the serving of food. || 53 ||

By seeing [the appearance of] wood and so forth, there will be mutual conflict, as if among members of an unprecedented species; whether on land or in water, in the house or in the forest, one who encounters such shall experience great fear and oppression by the king for one year.
Its pacification is as follows: a vessel made of clay filled with molasses, with copper, bell-metal, or iron as the sacrificial fee (dakṣiṇā).
The gift of a red cloth and food. || 54 ||
Then, due to a great conflagration that broke the embankments of rivers, tanks, and ponds, the sacrificer met his death within a single year.

For that [rite], there is again a fire-offering for pacification (*śānti-homa*) using two types of mustard seeds, lac, sesame, *saṃvoḍi*, iron, silver, bronze, lead, *āḍharūṣa*, *sinduvāli*, *vaikaṅkata*, *paṇāśrī*, *sāhu*, *devadāru*, red [substances], goat, gold, consecration, food, meat, fish, and wine as the drink at the end. 57.

If, at the time of giving, the sacrificial deity becomes dissatisfied because the gift substance has not reached the recipient's hand, there will be death within one year due to cow-dung [contamination] during the rite; or, for the sacrificer, there will be death, separation, or the loss of son or wife.
To pacify this, the gift of a cow (godāna) must be performed again.
The gift of land, gold, and food. || 58 ||
Sometimes, for the theft of gold, there is the exhaustion of life-force, the giving of pacifying gold, and food.
By obtaining even a few pieces of gold, disease brings about loss. || 57 ||
If one does not see the light within one's own body for one year, there is danger of death and disease;
by means of the *Śāntidarpaṇa*, a person endowed with faith should give food as a gift, and a gift of sixteen *raktikās* of silver should be established. || 58 ||
If the death of the master occurs due to the acquisition of envy within the house or garden, that result is the arrival of a serpent’s abode accompanied by terrible pains;

one should perform a fire-oblation (homa) for its pacification according to the ritual of the worship of the water-pot (kalaśa), and [perform] the gift of a golden image of the Sun and Hiranyagarbha, as well as the consecration of silver. 59.

If the head, hands, feet, shanks, or other limbs of a deceased person are obtained within twelve days of death in one's house, death will occur after two years, and there will be danger to the wife; however, he shall live.

For the Śāntimahābali, the meat-bhoma, the jar-offering (kalaśapūjā), and the food offering (naivedya): thirty (30) pieces of dried meat (khāla), one egg (aṇḍaja), a black banner, a red cloth, gold for the gift, ghee, sesame seeds, white sesame, dūrvā grass, and one hundred (100) fruits;
one hundred and eight (108) grains of rice, a white flag, and one hundred and eight (108) copper vessels filled with ghee as gifts.
Accompanied by the solar disc, established in gold, with food, drink, and the giving of garments—one hundred and eight [offerings]. 72.

In a garden or near a house, by means of sugarcane, plantains, or sesame, or through the appearance of flowers, there is destruction for the king; by the flowering of sugarcane, there is the destruction of the husband within one year, or at the end of the rainy season.
For the sake of pacification, one should perform the worship of the water-pot at the site of the portent; having fashioned a gift in the form of gold, it should be given along with food.

If the fire in one's house or temple consumes its own body, death will not occur for five years; for that person, one should perform a peace-offering (*śānti-homa*), offering seven types of grain, seven types of fuel-sticks, clarified butter, and milk-rice (*pāyasa*).
One should perform the gift of gold and food according to one's capacity within seven days. || 62 ||
Through the sound of "anāsa" in the house, there is the entry of inauspicious deities, the death of the master, and the onset of disease for five years;
[this is averted] by the offering of propitiatory oblations (śānti-vali), the worship of Gaṇapati, and the recitation of the Stavarāja. || 63 ||

One should perform fumigation within the house, the waving of lamps, and the distribution of food among the family; for two years, one should offer the great oblation (mahābali) for peace, recite the chapter on pacification (śāntikādhyāya), and worship Durgā. || 64 ||

If a rainbow falls upon a house, there is danger of death within one year and the loss of wealth; for its pacification, one should perform a great offering (mahābali), a vigil for Gaṇeśa, and give gifts of gold and land. || 65 ||
If there is constant weeping by one's own dogs at the site of the house, there will be disease and grief for one year;
therefore, the offering of a propitiatory oblation (śānti-bali), the worship of Kūmāli, and the feeding of one's own dogs should be performed as the best remedy.

At the time of the fire sacrifice (homa), [the fire] filled with rice-grains [is auspicious], whereas it is inauspicious if it is devoid of fuel, foul-smelling, emitting sparks, excessively smoky, or turning to the left. 74.
Thus ends the *Śrīmṛtyuñjayakalpa*, which effects the pacification of the fruits of all calamities.
In the case of the night, the *mandahorās* are as follows: for the Sun, six; for the Moon, four; for Mars, two; for Mercury, seven; for Jupiter, five; for Venus, three;
and for Saturn, one. This applies to each respective night. In the case of the day, however, the order is reversed. For the Sun, six; for the Moon, four; for Mars, two;
for Mercury, seven; for Jupiter, five; for Venus, three; and for Saturn, one. Thus, the *mandahorās* are determined for each day and night.

1 damārāmadṛmādedaiśa rāmāmedaśadarā || darārāmamadārārāmadegaṇa bhāci ca || Samvat 840, Vaiśākha, dark fortnight, 2nd day, Thursday; written by Dunaka, the son of Daivajña Gauvaliśaṅkhara. Auspicious!
And for one year, with one-pointed concentration, the propitiation of Gaṇapati brings about peace; that indeed is the sphere of attainment. (69)

For one who has attained silver, and has further acquired many things such as gold, iron, bronze, lead, copper, jewels, crowns, and so forth, there may be the destruction of grief or its pacification; that itself constitutes the offering of objects and the worship of the chosen deity. (70)

If [the plant] is planted with jasmine flowers or other blossoms produced from different flowers, or if it bears fruit, one dies within six months; however, if it is established in a vessel of *kāśa* grass for the sake of peace, containing the image of the moon, along with gold and food for guests, [this evil is averted]. 71.

If one encounters this [disease] at a pond, a well, or through water-channels, or if it occurs while bathing in this [water], there is danger of death within one year. To pacify this, one should perform worship of the *kalaśa* (vase) and worship of the *nāga* (serpent) in a sanctuary of peace, offering five oblations (*bali*) consisting of *pārāvasu*, *priyaṅgu*, and so forth.
And by means of the propitiation of Śāntigaṇapati with one-pointed concentration for one year, that very attainment becomes his object. || 69 ||
